memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the shares, bullish on the business; conviction medium, a working hypothesis at Triaging depth. The record parks the case on the return, not on the gate: no D or F sits on management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4 is B), business quality (E 2, BB 2 is C), predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4 is B) or trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4 is B). Two triggers progress it to Early-Stage: a price at or below about 500p (the level at which the modal path clears a 20 percent-a-year return over eighteen months at a 12.4x multiple; about 440p on the three-year test), or evidence at the H1 FY2027 results on 5 November 2026 that the data-centre line held with the largest customer's share stable and cash conversion recovering above 70 percent, which would move the data-centre odds from even to probable and the multiple applied from 12.4x toward 14x. Nothing invalidates the case at this stage; the record says it becomes a case at a price about a fifth lower, or on evidence that the data-centre line is contracted rather than spot.
case: Thesis, as the record states it: Volex is a self-help compounder with a cyclical overlay, and the price has moved before we can. Ten years of guiding under and delivering over have taken the margin from 2 percent to 10.2 percent; the last year's doubling of high-speed copper sales to hyperscalers has carried that change through the whole chain into the sell-side's numbers and the share price. At 635.0p, about 14 times the earnings two years out and the 84th percentile of the stock's own multiple history, the modal return of about 5 to 7 percent a year does not clear the 20 percent bar, because the one leg that would carry it, the multiple holding while the largest customer keeps spending, is an even bet that the price already assumes.

The change forces (E 1, BB 1, B). External forces C: the one force of 'Demand Inflection' strength (hyperscaler spending on copper inside the AI rack; hyperscaler capital expenditure projected at 1.00 trillion USD in 2026; Active Electrical Cables at a 43 percent compound rate 2024 to 2029; Volex at 1.6 Tbps) acts on about a fifth of revenue, while Consumer and Medical (a third of revenue) face live headwinds and competition is tightening in the growth line itself (second-tier suppliers including Volex price 5 to 8 percent below Amphenol and TE Connectivity; Wistron classifies Volex as a reliable but limited secondary supplier; Huatai expects Amphenol to become sole supplier of copper connections for Nvidia AI systems; Credo litigation names Volex). Direction by force: demand a tailwind in data centre, defense and off-highway and a headwind in Consumer and Medical; competition D; disruption C (copper extended to 800G and 1.6T by retimers, favoured inside the rack on power; optics and co-packaged optics the later negative, the risks report's highest-plausibility failure pathway); political and regulatory C (12 percent of revenue exposed to US tariffs, 100 percent passed through; Turkish tax de-indexing for 2025 to 2027, a 4.2 USDm charge); supply side D (copper +32 percent to 13,303 USD per tonne in June 2026; Turkish wages rising twice a year; pass-through with a one-to-two-month lag); own cycle B (organic growth accelerating three years; H2 FY2026 +15.9 percent); macro C; catch-all B (Main Market admission, FTSE 250 eligibility). Internal forces B: guidance raised A (twice within FY2026, revenue to at least 1,220 USDm against 1,173 USDm consensus and operating profit to at least 122 USDm against 114.8 USDm, then beaten at 1,242.6 USDm and 127.3 USDm; the 9 to 10 percent corridor replaced by a 10 percent floor and a 12 percent target); strategy B (the plan scaled, resourced with 26 USDm into five Centres of Excellence, 25 USDm at San Luis Potosí, a 400 USDm facility; the June 2022 plan delivered a year early); acquisitions B (Kepler; twelve deals for about 400 USDm since FY2019 at a blended 5.2x EBITDA and a 15.3 percent EBITA return; the TT Electronics approach at 135.5p withdrawn on price; Murat Ticaret, up to 196 USDm, missed its second-year earn-out and required three Turkish site closures); new products B; new geographies B; balance sheet B (leverage 0.8x to 1.1x; target 1.0x to 2.0x); catch-all B (Main Market; 1.55 million LTIP options); standards C (cash conversion fell; Murat sites 58 percent of lost-time accidents); price rises C (nominal pass-throughs); shareholder returns C; other leaders C; perimeter C; chief executive D (a change of title, not of person). No screen red flag trips. Propagation: all six layers of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain, to consensus EPS for the first forecast year +33.5 percent in twelve months, which is precisely why the price has moved.

The financial outputs (E 2, BB 1, B). Sell-side upgrades B: the record, the revisions and the sell-side's own framing (Zeus excludes the 12 percent target on purpose; Jefferies 3 percent above consensus; Deutsche Bank the caution on non-recurrence) make further upgrades over six to twelve months more likely than not; upgrade record A; dashboard revisions A; guidance versus consensus B (medium-term guidance above consensus for every year; no numeric near-term guidance beyond the floor); guidance conservatism B; revision skew B; our modal forecast C (FY2027 EPS about 0.51 USD, at consensus 0.512 USD, above the floor; no Viewforth model, our own estimate stands in). Goldilocks growth B: about +17 percent FY2027, 14.0 percent a year to FY2028, 13.1 percent a year to FY2029, inside the band on all horizons; not A because the band is met on one line with one-to-two-year contracts against a +100 percent comparison. Key metrics C: margin B (9.8 to 10.2 to 10.6 percent in H2 FY2026; consensus 10.9 to 11.2 percent; levers named); revenue growth C (high but not rising; consensus +11.0, +7.5, +6.5 percent; the plan implies about 9 percent a year organic); cash conversion D (63.9 percent from 67.2; H1 free cash flow conversion 33.4 percent; inventory +36 percent to 269.1 USDm, finished goods 118.2 USDm from 74.1 USDm; receivable days 72 from 62; working capital outflow 55.2 USDm against 18.1 USDm; consensus free cash flow 38.1 USDm FY2027 below FY2026's 42.3 USDm, then 63.6 and 79.0 USDm); net debt C (leverage rising for accretive uses; interest cover 10.4x; a 39 percent revenue fall to breach covenants). Staircase B: near steps (September 2026 FTSE 250 review; 5 November 2026 results; the buyback; a possible acquisition), mid steps (FY2027 results June 2027; San Luis Potosí commissioning; Spokane-to-Irvine; battery storage; the Medical margin test at 9 percent by H2 FY2027; the 300 USDm leg), far steps C (the 12 percent margin; North American off-highway at 100 to 200 USDm; 1.6T ramps; 2.0 billion USD by FY2030).
counter_case: The strongest case against, at Building Block 4 and carried at Building Blocks 1 to 3, is the risks report's FALSE FRIEND profile, the hypothesis its analysis of competing hypotheses scores with the fewest inconsistencies (two hard inconsistencies against five for the bull thesis). The operating metrics are strong because one hyperscaler doubled its orders in a year in which competitors could not deliver, under a hub model that put 71 USDm of extra inventory on Volex's balance sheet. That customer treats Volex as a secondary source for capacity and price, holds it to one-to-two-year contracts, and can shift allocation to Amphenol as supply loosens or to optics as speeds rise. When it does, revenue growth falls to the mid-single digits the other four segments deliver, the margin slips back toward the 10 percent floor as the most profitable line shrinks, cash conversion does not recover because the inventory was built for volumes that do not come, and the multiple returns to the ten-year median of about 10x, a fall of a quarter on earnings that are also falling. The evidence for it: the largest customer from 8 to 18.7 percent of revenue in one year; Deutsche Bank's and Jefferies' own caution that FY2026's data-centre volumes were partly customer pull-forward and competitors' capacity shortfalls that may not recur; Wistron's classification of Volex as a reliable but limited secondary supplier; Huatai's expectation that Amphenol becomes sole supplier of copper connections for Nvidia AI systems; cash conversion at 63.9 percent and receivable days at 72; the Murat earn-out miss as a sign that integration is harder than presented; and the company's own history, in which Apple was a third of sales in 2012 and its redesign contributed to a 93 percent share-price fall from February 2010 to June 2016. Its second form, at Building Block 3: the "proven upgrader" record coincides with a decade of margin recovery from 2 percent that is now complete, and the last year's upgrades were a single customer's doubling; the pattern may be a demand spike wearing a compounder's clothes, and the sell-side's conservatism may be a correct reading rather than mis-modelling. Its third form, at Building Block 2: read against the connector leaders rather than UK metal-bashers, Volex is a second-tier assembler with pass-through pricing and a working-capital cycle its largest customer dictates, and the foundations are not robust at all because the growth line belongs to the customer and the margin belongs to the mix the customer chooses. Its fourth form, at Building Block 1: the change is a continuation of a ten-year self-help the market has now fully recognised, and if the customer's spending normalises the multiple returns to its two-year median of 12.0x or lower.

The record concedes: the doubling was partly a capacity event; the contracts are short; the customer holds the power and the working capital shows it; the multiple at the 84th percentile leaves no cushion for a miss; the modal return fails the bar at this price on the record's own arithmetic; the FY2026 upgrades were concentrated in one line and one customer; the margin recovery from 2 to 10 percent cannot be repeated; and the brokers were right to exclude the 300 USDm of acquisitions until bought. This is why the thesis is D, the case is D, and the recommendation is to wait.
triggers: - Progress trigger one: the price at or below about 500p (the eighteen-month bar-clearing level on the modal path at 12.4x; about 440p on the three-year test); a multiple falling toward 12x on unchanged earnings restores the case at the same earnings.

- Progress trigger two: the H1 FY2027 results on 5 November 2026 showing Complex Industrial Technology still growing, the largest customer's share stable or lower, and cash conversion recovering above 70 percent; this moves the data-centre odds from even to probable and the multiple applied from 12.4x toward 14x.

- The first thing to check next (the earnings review's own point): the proportion of data-centre revenue under multi-year commitment, which is not disclosed; disclosure that a material part is contracted would move the view.

- The margin: Medical margin back above 9 percent by H2 FY2027 and a first-half group margin above 11 percent would change the view on 12 percent from possible to probable; alarm below 10.0 percent in a half; invalidate below 9.5 percent.

- The largest customer: alarm above 20 percent of revenue; invalidate a reported decline in Complex Industrial Technology revenue. Data-centre revenue (about 236 USDm FY2026): alarm a first-half decline; invalidate a halving.

- Cash conversion (63.9 percent): modal above 75 percent in FY2027; alarm below 70 percent; invalidate below 60 percent with inventory rising faster than revenue. Net working capital (28.4 percent of revenue): alarm rising again at H1 FY2027.

judgement.heading: Volex | Middle Innings Core Investment, no sell signal | 4.42% of the fund's capital in 2 tranches
judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** Volex is in Industrials and capital goods. Industrials and capital goods' Industry RS was 46 at the Friday 23 October reading (73 four weeks earlier)
- **Sector:** Volex is in Engineered components, polymers and electronics manufacturing. That sector's Sector RS was 73 at the 30 September month-end (61 at the August month-end)
  - Volex's sector's other companies, with their daily Stock RS: Senior (84, in the Pool of Stocks Eligible for Middle Innings Portfolio Selection), DiscoverIE (80, in the Pool), MTU Aero Engines (23), SKF (67), Trelleborg (75), SFS Group (74), and 9 more
- **Cohort:** Volex is in Electronic components and connectivity makers. The cohort's relative strength was 69 on Friday's daily reading (93 four weeks earlier). Volex's cohort's other companies: DiscoverIE (80), Huber + Suhner (21), Solid State (35), TT Electronics (98)
- **Volex's charts are on Volex's page on the PMS Per-stock Dashboard:** https://vfhqi.github.io/ratings/pms/holding.html?t=VLX-GB

**What is going on, and why it matters**
- **The price move, by beta:** over five sessions Volex's shares fell about 16% while the Stoxx Europe 600 fell about 1.4%; Volex's beta of 1.58 explains about 2% of the fall, so Volex's own move was about -14%, 2.3 times its usual size, which is unusual
  - The dated news: Volex's half-year trading update on Monday 19 October guided first-half revenue to at least 710 million dollars (about 22% higher than a year earlier) and full-year operating profit to the top end of expectations, and said growth is normalising as last year's surge in data-centre orders drops out of the comparison; Volex fell 11.6% that day
  - Jefferies and Berenberg raised their target prices for Volex after the update, and Volex completed a 20 million pound share buyback during the week
- **The sector:** Volex's sector's companies fell about 2% over the same five sessions, so the Volex fall is Volex's own; the market is now paying less for companies that grew on data-centre demand
- **The analysts:** for Volex, Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates (of the analysts with a next-year sales estimate, the share who raised it in the last 100 days minus the share who cut it) and Net Upgrade Breadth, target prices were both +100% at the 30 September month-end
  - Volex has no daily analysts' readings in our data, so the effect of the trading update on Volex's estimates is not yet measured

**What it means for the position**
- **Holding:** hold Volex to the 30 October month-end reading; no Sell Criterion is met at the readings the rule uses, and Volex passes every test of the Pool of Stocks Eligible for Middle Innings Portfolio Selection at the 30 September month-end
- **Selling:** Volex's relative 52W high trigger is at about 529.8p, about 1% below Friday's close of 536.0p; if Volex's relative price is more than 25% below its 52-week high at the 30 October month-end, the whole Volex holding is sold at the 3 November session. I put that at about even
- **Adding:** no add; Volex is below its 50-day moving average (614.2p), which is no longer rising, so neither of your add tests is met, and the memo's buying price (about 500p) is below the relative 52W high trigger

**What we could lose:** about 0.05% of the fund's capital, if Volex's price falls to its relative 52W high trigger; the figure is small only because Volex has already fallen most of the way to that trigger

**Experiment: which stocks Volex's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)
- **Oxford Instruments** (same country of listing): 0.68 and 0.62, strong
- **DiscoverIE** (same sector, cohort and country of listing): 0.58 and 0.46, strong
- **Halma** (same country of listing): 0.57 and 0.48, strong
- **AQ Group** (same sector): 0.52 and 0.51, strong
- **My reading:** Volex trades with United Kingdom precision-electronics names, but last week's fall was Volex's own news; watch DiscoverIE, the one strong partner in Volex's cohort, for whether the market extends the data-centre worry to the group

**The Investment Analyst's memo on Volex (1 October, at 635.0p; digest of 23 September)**
- **Decided:** the memo on Volex parks the case on the return, not on the quality gate; the memo is neutral on the shares and bullish on the business
- **Must happen:** at the first-half results in November, Complex Industrial Technology still growing, the largest customer's share stable or lower, and cash conversion back above 70%
- **Main risk:** the "false friend" profile: one hyperscale customer doubled its orders in a year competitors could not deliver
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** clears our bar of 20% a year only at or below about 500p, about 7% below Friday's close
- **Next test:** the 30 October month-end reading, then Volex's first-half results in November

**My judgement:** neutral on the Volex position, low to medium conviction
- The trading update confirmed the memo's main risk in words (data-centre growth normalising) while the numbers stayed good, and the market sold Volex on the words; the rule, not my view, now decides Volex at the 30 October reading
- **Counter-case:** the fall may already price the normalisation, with Volex now within about 7% of the memo's buying price and two brokers raising targets; a recovery of a few percent before 30 October keeps Volex in the book

**What would change my view:** Volex's relative price at the 30 October month-end; the first-half results against the memo's three tests
